gaps.name: Draft preview in the chat list row
gaps.whatItIs: A chat with an unsent draft shows a red "Draft:" prefix and the draft text in the subtitle line, overriding the last message.
gaps.whyItMatters: Without it there is no way to see from the chat list which conversations still have something half-written; the user has to open every chat to find it. TGClient.m already exposes chat["draft"] and TGSavedMessagesViewController already renders it for topics, so the chat list is the odd one out.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/TGChatListViewController.m cell subtitle rendering; data already comes from src/TGClient.m:2350 (info["draft"]) and is documented in src/TGClient+ChatList.h:240.
tdlib: updateChatDraftMessage (already handled in TGClient.m chat info mapping)

gaps.name: Draft saved on backgrounding and termination
gaps.whatItIs: The composer draft is flushed to TDLib whenever the app resigns active or is about to terminate, not only when the chat screen is popped.
gaps.whyItMatters: Today saveDraft runs only in -viewWillDisappear (src/TGChatViewController.m:1675). Home-button out of a chat and let iOS 6 jetsam kill the app - which happens constantly on a 512MB 4S - and the typed text is gone. This is the single most common way a draft is lost on this hardware.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/AppDelegate.m (applicationDidEnterBackground / applicationWillTerminate) calling into the visible TGChatViewController, or an NSNotification observer added in src/TGChatViewController.m next to restoreDraft.
tdlib: setChatDraftMessage - already wrapped as -setDraftText:replyTo:inChat:thread: in TGClient+Messages.h:185

gaps.name: Custom date and time picker for scheduling
gaps.whatItIs: ChatScheduleTimeController presents a wheel picker for any date/time, with a minimum time and a "Send when online" branch; the presets are shortcuts on top of it, not the whole feature.
gaps.whyItMatters: We only offer In 1 Hour / In 8 Hours / Tomorrow Morning / When Online (src/TGChatViewController.m runSendOption). Anything else - a birthday message next week, a post at 18:00 tomorrow - is impossible. UIDatePicker exists on iOS 6, so the only reason it is missing is that nobody built the sheet.
gaps.whereItGoes: A small UIDatePicker sheet reachable from the "Schedule Message" branch in src/TGChatViewController.m runSendOption:, feeding self.scheduledSendDate.
tdlib: messageSchedulingStateSendAtDate via the existing sendOptionsDictionary "sendDate" key (TGClient+Messages.h:20)

gaps.name: Real scheduled-messages screen with reschedule, edit and delete
gaps.whatItIs: The modern client opens the chat in a scheduled mode: the pending messages are shown as normal bubbles, ordered by send time, each with a context menu offering Send Now, Reschedule, Edit and Delete.
gaps.whyItMatters: Ours is a flat UIActionSheet listing scheduled messages, and the only action is Send Now (showScheduledMessages / sendScheduledMessageAtIndex in src/TGChatViewController.m). A scheduled message with the wrong time or a typo can only be sent immediately or left to fire wrong - it cannot be moved or cancelled. rescheduleMessage is already wrapped and unused by any UI.
gaps.whereItGoes: A new lightweight list screen pushed from the send-options sheet, or reuse of TGChatViewController in a scheduled mode; actions via src/TGMessageActionsSheet.m.

gaps.name: Scheduled-messages entry point outside the long-press
gaps.whatItIs: When a chat has pending scheduled messages the modern client shows a clock button in the navigation bar so the pending queue is visible and reachable at a glance.
gaps.whyItMatters: Our only route to scheduled messages is a long-press on Send, and the row only appears if the list happens to be loaded. A user who scheduled something yesterday has no signal it is still pending and no obvious way back to it.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/TGChatViewController.m navigation bar, driven by the existing self.scheduledMessages array populated by loadScheduledMessages.

gaps.name: Live refresh when a scheduled message fires or is changed elsewhere
gaps.whatItIs: TDLib pushes updateNewMessage / updateDeleteMessages for the scheduled queue and updateChatDraftMessage when another device edits the draft; the modern client reacts to both.
gaps.whyItMatters: loadScheduledMessages runs once on open, and restoreDraft is guarded by draftRestored so it never runs twice. A message that fires while the chat is open leaves a stale entry in our list, and a draft typed on another device never appears - or worse, our stale composer text overwrites it on exit.
gaps.whereItGoes: The update dispatch in src/TGClient.m plus the handlers in src/TGChatViewController.m (restoreDraft / loadScheduledMessages).

gaps.name: Reminders in Saved Messages
gaps.whatItIs: In Saved Messages the scheduling UI is relabelled as reminders - "Set a reminder", a reminders list - and the fired message arrives as a notification to yourself.
gaps.whyItMatters: This is the cheapest genuinely useful scheduling use case on a phone that is mostly used for messaging, and it is the one place the wording matters: "Schedule Message" to yourself reads as nonsense. The mechanism is identical to what we already have.
gaps.whereItGoes: Wording and entry point in src/TGSavedMessagesViewController.m and the send-options sheet in src/TGChatViewController.m when chatId is the self chat.

gaps.name: Draft carries formatting, reply target and media caption
gaps.whatItIs: A TDLib draftMessage holds a full formattedText with entities, an input_message_reply_to and can survive an attachment caption, not just a plain string.
gaps.whyItMatters: We store and restore plain text plus a reply id, and restoreDraft only shows a generic "Reply to message" banner without the quoted message. Bold/link markup and any caption typed under an attachment are silently dropped when the chat is reopened.
gaps.whereItGoes: src/TGClient+Messages.m setDraftText/draftForChat (widen to formatted text) and the compose banner restore in src/TGChatViewController.m restoreDraft.
tdlib: setChatDraftMessage with draftMessage.input_message_text.text.entities (currently sent as plain text)

gaps.name: Message effects on send
gaps.whatItIs: A Premium sender picks an effect next to the send button and the recipient's client plays a full-screen animation over the bubble.
gaps.whyItMatters: A user would notice effects arriving from modern clients and nothing happening, but there is no fix: the payload is a TGS/webm animation and effect_id can only be set by an active Premium account.
gaps.whereItGoes: Would be the send-options sheet in src/TGChatViewController.m; already catalogued as blocked and correctly so.
